item.title: One Pair Across Every Shot

turns.text: Make a realistic, silent 15-second widescreen story in three shots: a woman with a freckled face and red pixie cut drops a red scarf; a man with a shaved head and round glasses picks it up; he returns it and they smile. Both adults, on a quiet street. Show both faces clearly in every shot and keep exactly the same two faces throughout—no changing actors between cuts.

item.tests: Maintains two distinct generated facial identities across three story shots, including shots where either character is the focus.

answer_sheet.Character identities: An adult woman with a freckled face and red pixie cut, and an adult man with a shaved head and round glasses. Invent their faces but keep each identity unchanged across all three shots.
answer_sheet.Face visibility: Both faces must be clearly visible in every shot, including when the scarf is dropped and picked up.
answer_sheet.Story and setting: On a quiet street, the woman drops a red scarf, the man picks it up, and he returns it before they smile at each other.
answer_sheet.Length and format: One 15-second widescreen 16:9 video in three shots.
answer_sheet.Style and mood: Realistic live action, a small friendly encounter.
answer_sheet.Sound and text: Silent, with no captions, titles or dialogue.

must_haves: One assembled 15-second 16:9 film tells the story in three distinct shots.
The woman retains the same facial structure, freckles and red pixie cut in all three shots.
The man retains the same facial structure, shaved head and round glasses in all three shots; the two identities never merge or swap.
Both faces are clearly visible in every shot, not hidden by rear views, distant framing or object-only cutaways.
The red scarf is dropped by the woman, picked up by the man and returned to her in that order, ending with mutual smiles.
The film looks realistic and has no audible soundtrack.

I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**The 15-second version is estimated at 360 credits**: three 5-second shots at 120 credits each, using free-plan-compatible **Minimax H3 at 480p**, widescreen 16:9, with no audio. Joining the shots costs no credits.

**Nothing has been generated or charged.** I can’t verify your remaining balance with the available tools.

### Important limitation
I **can’t guarantee exactly identical faces across all three shots**. Using each shot’s final frame to start the next helps preserve both actors, but facial details can still drift. Showing both faces clearly while the man bends to retrieve the scarf is also a difficult constraint. If exact identity continuity is non-negotiable, I wouldn’t recommend spending credits on this generation.

### Cheaper options
At the same quoted rate of 24 credits per second:

| Version | Estimated credits | Trade-off |
|---|---:|---|
| 15 seconds, three shots | **360** | More room for the actions |
| 9 seconds, three 3-second shots | **216** | Faster pacing |
| 6 seconds, three 2-second shots | **144** | Likely rushed, especially the return and smiles |

**480p is already the lowest resolution offered by this production route.** Shortening the video reduces cost; keeping it silent avoids audio charges. Any retries would cost extra.

My recommendation is a **single 5-second test shot for 120 credits**, then stop for your review before making the rest. That limits the initial spend but doesn’t guarantee later continuity.

Would you prefer the test, the 9-second version, or no generation given the identity risk?

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Photorealistic live-action shot on a quiet street in soft natural daylight. One adult woman with a clearly freckled face and a red pixie haircut stands beside one adult man with a shaved head and round glasses. Eye-level frontal medium-wide two-shot, both faces clearly visible, in focus, unobstructed and recognizable throughout. The woman drops a red scarf from her hand onto the pavement while the man remains standing beside her. One continuous shot, stable camera, no cuts, no additional people, no captions or on-screen words. End with both adults still in frame and both faces clearly visible, holding still for the final second. Silent.
